The engineering behind it

The demo explains the loop.
The repository must prove it.

HOWDY Dev Day asks for both: a working product and a reproducible agentic engineering process. The story above maps to the six required capabilities; the submission still needs real artifacts.

Intent + specification

Requirements, architecture, constraints, and definition of done.

Required evidence: engineering spec Context engineering

Scoped instructions, tools, source references, and handoffs.

Inspect repository instructions ↗ Orchestration + parallel work

Independent scopes, dependencies, and integration points.

Inspect the orchestration core ↗ Harness + backpressure

Tests, type checks, builds, and rendered acceptance.

Inspect validation scripts ↗ Autonomous loops + recovery

A real failure, correction, and recheck without a new human prompt.

Required evidence: a recorded closed loop Human as orchestrator

The engineer chooses scope, constraints, tradeoffs, and readiness.

Inspect this website’s review ↗

Submission format: up to 3 minutes, with roughly 90 seconds on the product and 90 seconds on how it was engineered. Interactive examples are not a substitute for the required execution evidence.

Local backbone

The session outlives the window.

A Rust daemon owns terminal sessions and workspace state. The Electron desktop is a view, not the lifetime of your work.

Bring your harness

Your agents. Your accounts.

Work with Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, or a plain shell. Drogon organizes execution; your configured harness connects to its provider.

Inspectable by default

Open source, down to the core.

MIT-licensed. No app telemetry or automatic updater in the preview. Tests and reproducible build instructions live with the code.
